import re
from datetime import time
from pathlib import Path

DATASET_DIR = Path("training_dataset")
# Filenames carry a timestamp, e.g. camera1_2024-01-15_0342.jpg
TIMESTAMP_RE = re.compile(r"(\d{4})-(\d{2})-(\d{2})[_-](\d{2})(\d{2})")

DAY_START = time(7, 0)
DAY_END = time(17, 0)


def is_nighttime(path):
    match = TIMESTAMP_RE.search(path.name)
    if match is None:
        return False
    hour, minute = int(match.group(4)), int(match.group(5))
    captured = time(hour, minute)
    return captured < DAY_START or captured >= DAY_END


images = sorted(
    p for p in DATASET_DIR.rglob("*") if p.suffix.lower() in {".jpg", ".jpeg", ".png"}
)
night_images = [p for p in images if is_nighttime(p)]

for path in night_images:
    path.unlink()

print(f"removed {len(night_images)} nighttime images of {len(images)} total")

import tkinter as tk

RENDER_DELAY_MS = 120


class ImageLabeler(tk.Tk):
    def __init__(self, image_paths):
        super().__init__()
        self.image_paths = image_paths
        self.index = 0
        self._render_job = None

        self.label = tk.Label(self)
        self.label.pack(fill="both", expand=True)
        self.bind("<Left>", lambda e: self.navigate(-1))
        self.bind("<Right>", lambda e: self.navigate(1))
        self.schedule_render()

    def navigate(self, delta):
        # Move the index immediately so rapid key presses stay responsive,
        # but coalesce the expensive render into a single trailing call.
        self.index = max(0, min(len(self.image_paths) - 1, self.index + delta))
        self.schedule_render()

    def schedule_render(self):
        if self._render_job is not None:
            self.after_cancel(self._render_job)
        self._render_job = self.after(RENDER_DELAY_MS, self.render)

    def render(self):
        self._render_job = None
        from PIL import Image, ImageTk

        image = Image.open(self.image_paths[self.index])
        self._photo = ImageTk.PhotoImage(image)
        self.label.configure(image=self._photo)
        self.title(f"{self.index + 1}/{len(self.image_paths)}")

"""flagged_review.py -- Tkinter review GUI for auto-flagged CV predictions.

Reuses the ROI drawing, 4-class label schema, and JSON/CSV save format from
cv_label_images.py. Reviewed items are moved to data/flagged/reviewed/.
"""

import csv
import json
import shutil
import tkinter as tk
from pathlib import Path

from PIL import Image, ImageDraw, ImageTk

FLAGGED_DIR = Path("data/flagged")
REVIEWED_DIR = FLAGGED_DIR / "reviewed"
LABELS = ["snowmaking", "no_snowmaking", "obscured", "lens_covered"]


def normalized(roi):
    x1, y1, x2, y2 = roi["x1"], roi["y1"], roi["x2"], roi["y2"]
    return min(x1, x2), min(y1, y2), max(x1, x2), max(y1, y2)


def load_flagged():
    return sorted(FLAGGED_DIR.glob("*.json"))


class FlaggedReview(tk.Tk):
    def __init__(self, records):
        super().__init__()
        self.title("Flagged Prediction Review")
        self.records = records
        self.index = 0
        self.reviewed = []

        self.canvas = tk.Label(self)
        self.canvas.pack(fill="both", expand=True)

        buttons = tk.Frame(self)
        buttons.pack(fill="x")
        for label in LABELS:
            tk.Button(
                buttons, text=label, command=lambda l=label: self.confirm(l)
            ).pack(side="left", expand=True, fill="x")

        REVIEWED_DIR.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
        self.show()

    def show(self):
        if self.index >= len(self.records):
            self.save_reviewed()
            self.destroy()
            return

        record = json.loads(self.records[self.index].read_text())
        image = Image.open(record["image_path"]).convert("RGB")
        draw = ImageDraw.Draw(image)
        for roi in record.get("rois", []):
            draw.rectangle(normalized(roi), outline="red", width=3)

        self._photo = ImageTk.PhotoImage(image)
        self.canvas.configure(image=self._photo)
        self.title(
            f"{self.index + 1}/{len(self.records)} -- "
            f"predicted {record['predicted_label']} "
            f"({record['confidence']:.2f})"
        )

    def confirm(self, label):
        path = self.records[self.index]
        record = json.loads(path.read_text())
        record["reviewed_label"] = label
        self.reviewed.append(record)

        (REVIEWED_DIR / path.name).write_text(json.dumps(record, indent=2))
        path.unlink()
        self.index += 1
        self.show()

    def save_reviewed(self):
        if not self.reviewed:
            return
        with (REVIEWED_DIR / "reviewed.csv").open("w", newline="") as fh:
            writer = csv.DictWriter(
                fh,
                fieldnames=["image_path", "predicted_label", "confidence", "reviewed_label"],
            )
            writer.writeheader()
            for record in self.reviewed:
                writer.writerow({k: record[k] for k in writer.fieldnames})


if __name__ == "__main__":
    FlaggedReview(load_flagged()).mainloop()

(x_train, y_train), (x_test, y_test) = tf.keras.datasets.mnist.load_data()

        tf.keras.layers.Dense(10, activation="softmax"),

    metrics=["accuracy"],
)

import matplotlib.pyplot as plt
import pandas as pd
from matplotlib.backends.backend_tkagg import FigureCanvasTkAgg


class HistogramViewer(tk.Tk):
    def __init__(self):
        super().__init__()
        self.title("CSV Histogram Viewer")
        self.df = None

        controls = tk.Frame(self)
        controls.pack(fill="x")
        tk.Button(controls, text="Open CSV...", command=self.open_csv).pack(side="left")

        self.column_box = ttk.Combobox(controls, state="readonly")
        self.column_box.pack(side="left", expand=True, fill="x")
        self.column_box.bind("<<ComboboxSelected>>", lambda e: self.plot())

        self.figure = plt.Figure(figsize=(6, 4), dpi=100)
        self.axes = self.figure.add_subplot(111)
        self.canvas = FigureCanvasTkAgg(self.figure, master=self)
        self.canvas.get_tk_widget().pack(fill="both", expand=True)

    def open_csv(self):
        path = filedialog.askopenfilename(filetypes=[("CSV files", "*.csv")])
        if not path:
            return
        self.df = pd.read_csv(path)
        numeric = list(self.df.select_dtypes("number").columns)
        if not numeric:
            messagebox.showerror("No numeric columns", "This CSV has no numeric columns.")
            return
        self.column_box["values"] = numeric
        self.column_box.current(0)
        self.plot()

    def plot(self):
        column = self.column_box.get()
        if self.df is None or not column:
            return
        self.axes.clear()
        self.axes.hist(self.df[column].dropna(), bins=30)
        self.axes.set_xlabel(column)
        self.axes.set_ylabel("count")
        self.canvas.draw()


if __name__ == "__main__":
    HistogramViewer().mainloop()

# KeyError: 'label' at train.py:42
#
# Cause: the training loop indexes batch["label"], but the dataset yields the
# column under a different name (e.g. "labels" after a HF collator, or the
# column was renamed/dropped upstream). A KeyError means the key is simply not
# in the batch -- so resolve the real name instead of guessing.

LABEL_KEYS = ("label", "labels", "target", "y")


def get_labels(batch):
    for key in LABEL_KEYS:
        if key in batch:
            return batch[key]
    raise KeyError(
        f"no label column in batch; available keys: {sorted(batch.keys())}"
    )


def train(model, dataloader, optimizer, loss_fn):
    model.train()
    for batch in dataloader:
        labels = get_labels(batch)          # was: batch["label"]  <- line 42
        outputs = model(batch["input_ids"])
        loss = loss_fn(outputs, labels)

        optimizer.zero_grad()
        loss.backward()
        optimizer.step()

"""scraper.py -- every requests call now sets an explicit timeout.

Without a timeout a request can hang indefinitely: requests has no default.
"""

import requests

TIMEOUT_SECONDS = 10


def fetch_page(url):
    response = requests.get(url, timeout=TIMEOUT_SECONDS)
    response.raise_for_status()
    return response.text


def post_result(url, payload):
    response = requests.post(url, json=payload, timeout=TIMEOUT_SECONDS)
    response.raise_for_status()
    return response.json()


def head_check(url, session=None):
    client = session or requests
    return client.head(url, timeout=TIMEOUT_SECONDS).status_code

import numpy as np
from datasets import load_dataset
from sklearn.metrics import accuracy_score, f1_score
from transformers import (
    AutoModelForSequenceClassification,
    AutoTokenizer,
    Trainer,
    TrainingArguments,
)

MODEL_NAME = "bert-base-uncased"

dataset = load_dataset("csv", data_files="support_tickets.csv")["train"]
dataset = dataset.class_encode_column("intent").train_test_split(test_size=0.2, seed=42)
num_labels = dataset["train"].features["intent"].num_classes

tokenizer = AutoTokenizer.from_pretrained(MODEL_NAME)
model = AutoModelForSequenceClassification.from_pretrained(
    MODEL_NAME, num_labels=num_labels
)


def tokenize(batch):
    return tokenizer(batch["text"], truncation=True, max_length=256)


tokenized = dataset.map(tokenize, batched=True).rename_column("intent", "labels")


def compute_metrics(eval_pred):
    logits, labels = eval_pred
    preds = np.argmax(logits, axis=-1)
    return {
        "accuracy": accuracy_score(labels, preds),
        "f1": f1_score(labels, preds, average="macro"),
    }


trainer = Trainer(
    model=model,
    args=TrainingArguments(
        output_dir="bert-intent",
        num_train_epochs=3,
        per_device_train_batch_size=16,
        learning_rate=2e-5,
        eval_strategy="epoch",
    ),
    train_dataset=tokenized["train"],
    eval_dataset=tokenized["test"],
    processing_class=tokenizer,
    compute_metrics=compute_metrics,
)
trainer.train()
trainer.save_model("bert-intent/final")

# IndexError: list index out of range in parse_logs.py
#
# Cause: the parser indexes lines[0] / fields[1] without first checking that
# the log file produced any lines (or that a line actually split into enough
# fields). An empty log file yields an empty list, so lines[0] raises.

from pathlib import Path


def parse_logs(path):
    lines = Path(path).read_text().splitlines()
    if not lines:
        print(f"{path} is empty; nothing to parse")
        return []

    entries = []
    for lineno, line in enumerate(lines, start=1):
        fields = line.split("\t")
        if len(fields) < 3:
            print(f"skipping malformed line {lineno}: {line!r}")
            continue
        timestamp, level, message = fields[0], fields[1], fields[2]
        entries.append({"timestamp": timestamp, "level": level, "message": message})
    return entries

NUM_CLASSES = 10
DEVICE = "cuda" if torch.cuda.is_available() else "cpu"

transform = transforms.Compose(
    [
        transforms.Resize((224, 224)),

    ]

model = models.resnet18(weights=models.ResNet18_Weights.DEFAULT)
for param in model.parameters():
    param.requires_grad = False
model.fc = nn.Linear(model.fc.in_features, NUM_CLASSES)
model = model.to(DEVICE)

loss_fn = nn.CrossEntropyLoss()
optimizer = optim.Adam(model.fc.parameters(), lr=1e-3)

for epoch in range(5):
    model.train()
    running = 0.0
    for images, labels in loader:
        images, labels = images.to(DEVICE), labels.to(DEVICE)
        loss = loss_fn(model(images), labels)

        optimizer.zero_grad()
        loss.backward()
        optimizer.step()
        running += loss.item() * images.size(0)
    print(f"epoch {epoch + 1}: loss {running / len(dataset):.4f}")

torch.save(model.state_dict(), "resnet18_dog_breeds.pt")

import json
import tkinter as tk
from pathlib import Path

TASKS_PATH = Path("tasks.json")


class TodoApp(tk.Tk):
    def __init__(self):
        super().__init__()
        self.title("To-Do")
        self.tasks = self.load_tasks()

        entry_row = tk.Frame(self)
        entry_row.pack(fill="x")
        self.entry = tk.Entry(entry_row)
        self.entry.pack(side="left", expand=True, fill="x")
        self.entry.bind("<Return>", lambda e: self.add_task())
        tk.Button(entry_row, text="Add", command=self.add_task).pack(side="left")

        self.listbox = tk.Listbox(self, height=15)
        self.listbox.pack(fill="both", expand=True)
        self.listbox.bind("<Double-Button-1>", lambda e: self.toggle_task())

        tk.Button(self, text="Delete", command=self.delete_task).pack(fill="x")

        self.protocol("WM_DELETE_WINDOW", self.on_close)
        self.refresh()

    def load_tasks(self):
        if TASKS_PATH.exists():
            return json.loads(TASKS_PATH.read_text())
        return []

    def save_tasks(self):
        TASKS_PATH.write_text(json.dumps(self.tasks, indent=2))

    def refresh(self):
        self.listbox.delete(0, tk.END)
        for task in self.tasks:
            mark = "x" if task["done"] else " "
            self.listbox.insert(tk.END, f"[{mark}] {task['text']}")

    def add_task(self):
        text = self.entry.get().strip()
        if not text:
            return
        self.tasks.append({"text": text, "done": False})
        self.entry.delete(0, tk.END)
        self.refresh()

    def selected_index(self):
        selection = self.listbox.curselection()
        return selection[0] if selection else None

    def toggle_task(self):
        index = self.selected_index()
        if index is None:
            return
        self.tasks[index]["done"] = not self.tasks[index]["done"]
        self.refresh()

    def delete_task(self):
        index = self.selected_index()
        if index is None:
            return
        del self.tasks[index]
        self.refresh()

    def on_close(self):
        self.save_tasks()
        self.destroy()


if __name__ == "__main__":
    TodoApp().mainloop()

        tk.Button(self, text="Choose folder...", command=self.choose_folder).pack(
            fill="x", padx=8, pady=4
        )

        tk.Label(size_row, text="Max width x height:").pack(side="left")

        self.width.insert(0, "800")
        self.width.pack(side="left")

        self.height.insert(0, "800")
        self.height.pack(side="left")

        tk.Button(self, text="Resize", command=self.resize_all).pack(
            fill="x", padx=8, pady=8
        )
        self.status = tk.Label(self, text="")
        self.status.pack(padx=8, pady=4)

    def choose_folder(self):
        folder = filedialog.askdirectory()
        if folder:
            self.folder = Path(folder)
            self.folder_label.configure(text=str(self.folder))

    def resize_all(self):
        if self.folder is None:
            messagebox.showerror("No folder", "Choose a folder first.")
            return
        try:
            size = (int(self.width.get()), int(self.height.get()))
        except ValueError:
            messagebox.showerror("Bad size", "Width and height must be integers.")
            return

        out_dir = self.folder / "resized"
        out_dir.mkdir(exist_ok=True)

        count = 0
        for path in self.folder.iterdir():
            if path.suffix.lower() not in SUFFIXES:
                continue
            with Image.open(path) as image:
                image.thumbnail(size)
                image.save(out_dir / path.name)
            count += 1

        self.status.configure(text=f"Resized {count} images into {out_dir}")


if __name__ == "__main__":
    ImageResizer().mainloop()

import requests
from tqdm import tqdm


def download(url, dest, chunk_size=8192):
    response = requests.get(url, stream=True, timeout=30)
    response.raise_for_status()
    total = int(response.headers.get("Content-Length", 0))

    with open(dest, "wb") as fh, tqdm(
        total=total or None,
        unit="B",
        unit_scale=True,
        desc=dest,
    ) as bar:
        for chunk in response.iter_content(chunk_size=chunk_size):
            fh.write(chunk)
            bar.update(len(chunk))

    return dest

# RuntimeError: working outside of application context
#
# Cause: Flask's app context is bound to the request-handling thread. A
# background thread started from a view has no context, so anything that
# touches `db`, `current_app`, or `g` raises. Pushing the context inside the
# thread -- with app.app_context() -- fixes it.

import threading

from flask import Flask, current_app

app = Flask(__name__)


def background_job(app):
    with app.app_context():
        # `db` / `current_app` are usable here because the context is pushed
        # in *this* thread, not inherited from the request thread.
        current_app.logger.info("running background job")
        db.session.execute(db.select(User))
        db.session.commit()


@app.route("/kick-off")
def kick_off():
    # Pass the real app object (not the `current_app` proxy) into the thread.
    threading.Thread(
        target=background_job, args=(current_app._get_current_object(),), daemon=True
    ).start()
    return "started", 202

# UnicodeDecodeError: 'utf-8' codec can't decode byte ...
#
# Cause: the CSV is not UTF-8 -- exports from Excel are usually cp1252 or
# utf-8-sig (UTF-8 with a BOM). pandas defaults to utf-8, so the first
# non-UTF-8 byte raises. Detect the encoding instead of guessing once.

import pandas as pd

ENCODINGS = ("utf-8", "utf-8-sig", "cp1252", "latin-1")


def load_csv(path):
    last_error = None
    for encoding in ENCODINGS:
        try:
            return pd.read_csv(path, encoding=encoding)
        except UnicodeDecodeError as exc:
            last_error = exc
    raise UnicodeDecodeError(
        last_error.encoding,
        last_error.object,
        last_error.start,
        last_error.end,
        f"{path} is not readable as any of {ENCODINGS}",
    )

# The while loop in scrape_all.py never terminates: it waits for a "next page"
# link that keeps coming back (the site clamps out-of-range pages to the last
# page), so the same page is fetched forever. Two guards fix it: stop when a
# page yields nothing new, and cap the total number of pages.

import requests

MAX_PAGES = 500


def scrape_all(base_url):
    results = []
    seen_urls = set()
    page = 1

    while page <= MAX_PAGES:
        url = f"{base_url}?page={page}"
        if url in seen_urls:
            break
        seen_urls.add(url)

        response = requests.get(url, timeout=10)
        response.raise_for_status()
        items = response.json()["items"]
        if not items:                       # no progress -> we are done
            break

        results.extend(items)
        page += 1
    else:
        print(f"stopped at the {MAX_PAGES}-page cap")

    return results

import shutil
import time
from pathlib import Path

from watchdog.events import FileSystemEventHandler
from watchdog.observers import Observer

WATCH_DIR = Path.home() / "Downloads"
DEST_DIR = Path.home() / "Documents" / "PDFs"


def unique_destination(name):
    target = DEST_DIR / name
    stem, suffix, counter = target.stem, target.suffix, 1
    while target.exists():
        target = DEST_DIR / f"{stem}-{counter}{suffix}"
        counter += 1
    return target


class PDFMover(FileSystemEventHandler):
    def on_created(self, event):
        if event.is_directory:
            return
        path = Path(event.src_path)
        if path.suffix.lower() != ".pdf":
            return

        # Wait for the writer to finish before moving a partially-written file.
        previous = -1
        while path.exists() and path.stat().st_size != previous:
            previous = path.stat().st_size
            time.sleep(0.5)

        destination = unique_destination(path.name)
        shutil.move(str(path), destination)
        print(f"moved {path.name} -> {destination}")


if __name__ == "__main__":
    DEST_DIR.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)

    observer = Observer()
    observer.schedule(PDFMover(), str(WATCH_DIR), recursive=False)
    observer.start()
    try:
        while True:
            time.sleep(1)
    except KeyboardInterrupt:
        observer.stop()
    observer.join()
